title: The ZigZag
reviewNotes: Three branches, 26 exact positions from the complete five-piece board. The source zigzag reaches Kb8 behind Kb6; after a8=Q Rxf7, Qa3 prevents ...Rf8 mate. Immediate f8=Q draws after the skewer. Qd5 reverses the outcome to a Black win; that selected source error stops at ...Rf8+ without inventing a full mating route.
transcript: Any white player would draw this, but only a true genius would be able to win from this position. You see, white is left with two pawns and black has an entire rook that it can use to try and stop them. For example, trying to get a queen would be a massive mistake. Now, after rook to F1 check, you have to move the king. You lose the queen and you lose the other pawn and this is a draw. But, white has foreseen a brilliant plan and it plays A7, now creating a dual threat of getting a queen. But, black is not that naive and it plays king to B6, now keeping contact with the pawn. Again, promoting would not work because of this check. And now, it might seem like we're free to move the king and prepare the promotion, but actually this fails to the brilliant shot king to C6. It might seem like we're free to get a new queen, but actually we're getting hit with the cold shower after rook to E1 check. The king and the rook collaborate in pushing the white king in front of the white queen and after it goes there, now rook to F1 is another skewer and the king is just in time to stop the white pawn from promoting and draw the game. So, is this it? Is this simply a draw? Well, not exactly. White has the brilliant king to E5, relinquishing control of the pawn, but the pawn can fend for himself. It's more important to stop the threats of the rook and king. And now, if the king tries to shoulder the white king again, we can promote with a check. So, black has nothing better to do but to check the white king. But, after some precise zigzagging, the king can re-route to the other side of the board and find shelter behind the black king. The king is in the way of his own ally. But, do not celebrate too soon because black does have one last trick. After rook to F1 and we promote to a queen, the rook can take and now we have to be very careful. Black is threatening a checkmate in one move and if we move the queen away, we are actually going to get checkmated very quickly. And if the king tries to run away, this is still going to be a skewer picking up the queen. But, luckily white has one move that holds everything together, queen to A3. From this position, the queen is defending the checking square and there is nothing left for black to do but to resign the game. If you love incredible chess, follow me for more.
